description:
## Goal

Give every production ordering of activation-bearing jobs, facts, waits, contribution transactions, and product completion waves one total typed semantic relation. The result must be independent of World-local Ty mint order, hash discovery order, display/Debug/TyCanon text, and reused binder-address tokens. This is a prerequisite extracted from fz-kdt.46; exact-edge accounting, cross-completion settlement batching, session accounting, product/report folding, and root-analysis work remain outside this ticket.

## Proven failures

- Raw Ty order reverses activation wake and diagnostic order under opposite mint histories.
- Display is non-injective: list(int) and non_empty_list(int) collide, and the live enum_predicate_search inventory retains six such empty/non-empty pairs inside distinct executable signatures.
- Closure-literal captures were not structurally addressed.
- One unscoped correlation map aliases an embedded captured a0 with an independent nested callable a0, while naive fresh-binder schemes break intentional arg/return/capture sharing and reduce the 59-executable inventory to 52.
- DeriveCallGraphComponent can emit the same derivations in different intra-completion order, redistributing RuntimeDemand settlement and downstream product causality.
- A producer can discover co-products in hash order and the driver can publish the requested anchor after its peers; producer-local sorting therefore cannot define one completion's publication order.
- ProductMemo reader invalidation/reconciliation and PullSession contribution replacement can recursively expose unordered work after an initially ordered key.
- IncomingInputRelations and OutgoingInputEdges formerly stored HashMap/HashSet-backed ProductValues, so one ordered ProductKey commit could still expose hash order while a formula read the immutable value.
- Terminal unresolved inventories and product fact waits retained raw activation-bearing ordering.

## Correct model

- Embedded values belong to the enclosing activation surface.
- Every ArrowSig introduces a binder scope. A capture shares that binder only when the same original participates in its args or return; otherwise the capture is re-owned under its exact Capture path. Sibling and nested binders are distinct, repeated variables within one binder remain correlated, and addressing is idempotent.
- SemanticOrd<Ctx>::semantic_cmp compares typed identities field by field. ActivationKey compares root, function, then arrow through Types::cmp_activation_ty; ExecutableKey, ExecutableSymbol, and TransportPosition form the single central comparator tree consumed by ProductKey and packaging. Job, FactKey, FactUse, terminal waits, contribution folds, and scheduler completion/publication delegate activation-bearing fields to that same relation.
- Types::cmp_activation_ty reuses ClauseOrder structural traversal in an ActivationArrow mode. That mode preserves the established activation precedence without parsing presentation: callable arguments, return, then literal; structural list emptiness and address paths break display collisions; callable literals compare by immutable owner-registered labels.
- Types owns an operation-tagged memo keyed by normalized (ActivationArrow, low Ty, high Ty). Reverse comparisons reuse the inverse. Interned descriptors, structural address paths, and callable labels are immutable for the Types/World lifetime, so no invalidation is needed. Labels are asserted present before caching and cannot be renamed. Hit/miss observation exists only under cfg(test).
- ClauseOrder retains a private storage-canonical relation used only to canonicalize DNF storage; it intentionally gives callable literals different precedence and is not exposed as an activation identity comparator. The test-only Types::cmp_ty accessor exists solely to classify the two relations.
- ProductReadContext stages every peer ProductKey/Value/dependency triple produced by one invocation. ProductDriver appends the requested key as the anchor. ProductMemo alone sorts and commits that complete same-producer completion envelope, installs all values before emitting changed-reader work, and owns the corresponding complete recursive-group commit. Graph discovery and producer loops establish membership only; they do not establish publication order. This envelope is ordering within one producer completion, not the forbidden fz-kdt.46 batching of independent fact settlements or pull completions.
- ProductMemo owns one semantic min-first typed mutation wave for pending/produced reader invalidation and refresh, fact movement reconciliation, stale-dependency choice, and artifact-product invalidation. Recursive work re-enters that same owner wave instead of sorting at each caller.
- PullSession separately owns a complete contribution transaction: it installs every caller replacement first, then recomputes the union of affected return/input targets in typed order. It does not fold one caller's hash traversal into observable settlement order.
- Activation-bearing immutable ProductValue collections are normalized once at construction. OutgoingEdgeFrontier is a sorted immutable executable slice; OutgoingInputEdges and IncomingInputRelations share a private OrderedIncomingInputs value with sorted slot/source slices; IncomingInputSlot exposes an immutable sorted source slice. Hash collections may exist only as ephemeral builders before that boundary.
- DependencyIndex owns typed Job and Publisher order for subscriber, waiter, reader, and unresolved-job waves, collecting multi-readiness readers raw and sorting once. Scheduler accepts one typed semantic context for the entire completion and wake wave and consumes those owner-returned vectors; it has no per-domain comparator callbacks. ContributionMap owns typed key order for touched and next-key join waves before any join can allocate.
- Public telemetry streams typed owner vectors for changed facts, movements, blocked waits, and stalled demanded facts; activation-input and work-graph HashSet projections sort the actual typed keys before rendering. JSON presentation never re-sorts rendered identities.
- TyCanon, display, Debug, and formatted strings remain presentation/testing tools only.

## TDD

1. Opposite Ty mint histories and opposite registration order give identical activation/job/fact/use/product-wait order, including display-colliding list and non_empty_list values.
2. Named closure captures compare identically across different local callable ids.
3. Same-token embedded and nested-binder a0 values do not alias; intentional arg/return/capture sharing, siblings, nesting, and repeated addressing remain exact.
4. One unique activation comparison misses once; repeated and reverse production comparisons hit the same typed memo entry.
5. The live executable census proves every distinct Eq identity compares non-Equal; equal-display pairs retain distinct raw Descr/address/callable-label evidence and strict inverse typed comparisons.
6. Opposite insertion plus every requested anchor gives one co-product commit sequence; a produced/pending reader diamond drains min-first; recursive groups commit one sequence for every anchor; PullSession caller/target/contributor transactions are canonical.
7. Opposite construction order gives identical immutable frontier, input-slot, and input-source iteration to downstream consumers.
8. Opposite-seed completion derivations, movements, publications, and wakes give identical typed order across repeated fresh processes.
9. Terminal unresolved diagnostics, transport behavior, native behavior, 59 executable inventory, canonical artifacts, and runtime answers remain pinned.
10. Static search proves production ordering does not call display, Debug formatting, TyCanon, StableSortKey/string helpers, or producer-local ordered publication APIs.

## Measured work effect

Typed activation order preserves fz_f98_range_map_converges at 226 AnalyzeActivation and 909 total evaluations. On enum_predicate_search it coalesces the second List.reduce_while_step/3 ReturnType ascent and the corresponding List.reduce_while_cont/3 ActivationInputs ascent into one causal window: that exact continuation formula moves from 10 to 9 runs, with one fewer content-caused changed-output run, identical four wakes and one blocked completion, no uncaused work, and every other formula-family total unchanged. The fixture ratchet therefore moves 538 to 537 AnalyzeActivation and 1351 to 1350 total.

On enum_take_drop_split, the typed schedule removes one transient CallSiteSummary retract/remint pair while preserving all 434 distinct identities: appearances/retractions move 450/16 to 449/15. Fourteen content-caused changed-output AnalyzeActivation runs coalesce across the same ascent without changing the eight unchanged runs; total evaluations move 2387 to 2373. Every other lifecycle, shift, formula-family, executable, artifact, and runtime gate must remain unchanged.

## Required deletion and boundary

Delete StableSortKey and all superseded display/Debug/canonical-string comparators, string parsing, separator encodings, blanket preserve-address modes, unscoped correlation attempts, raw FactKey Ord, temporary probes, producer-local semantic sorts/publication closures, Tarjan dependency-order plumbing, per-boundary reader sorts, and duplicate tests/docs. Keep a formula-evaluation member sort only if it is separately named and proven necessary for formula scheduling. Do not include fz-kdt.46 wait-edge storage, cross-completion settlement batching, wake arbitration, session accounting, product/report folding, or root-analysis changes.

## Acceptance

One typed, memoized, binder-scoped ActivationArrow relation owns activation-bearing identity order. ProductMemo owns the complete same-producer commit and reader-mutation waves; PullSession owns complete contribution replacement; immutable ProductValues own their activation-bearing member order at construction. No raw intern/hash identity or presentation string determines production order. Addressing is total, non-aliasing, correlated, and idempotent. Final semantic facts, diagnostics, executable inventory, backend/native artifacts, transport, and runtime behavior are identical; only the causally attributed, non-increasing work reductions above may move. Focused addressing/ordering/owner-wave/value/completion/transport tests, repeated exact cross-process gates, library/CLI/matrix gates, formatting, strict clippy, and current-base replay pass.

Full mixed kdt46 source remains untouched in /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-wt-kdt46; recoverable tree object 99ec12ece363a7a4c9d66902f00ee7c2b212ceaf captures the post-v10 binder-scope state before partition.

Design correction approved during implementation: canonical/display strings are forbidden as production order keys. Use the existing typed structural Types comparison after complete binder-scoped addressing, and propagate typed comparators through Job/FactKey/FactUse/scheduler consumers. The string-key attempt is rejected and must be deleted before review.

Performance/correctness refinement: interned Ty values are immutable, so the typed World-owned comparison relation must memoize each operation/type-pair outcome. Reversed pairs reuse the inverse where valid. Production sorting consumes typed Ordering from this memo; tests/telemetry prove one miss per unique pair and subsequent hits. Callable labels must be registered and stable before a comparison is cached. No rendered/canonical string is an identity or ordering surrogate.

Concrete completion-order RED from fz-kdt.5: opposite process seeds preserve the full 2,978 applied scheduler sequence but reverse DeriveCallGraphComponent canonical-definition emission inside one completion, then reorder RuntimeDemand recursive settlements and downstream product causality. Typed completion ordering must make these activation-bearing derivations/publications identical across seeds.

title: Give activation facts one binder-scoped semantic order
